description: Dialogue for Guildmaster Vorn who runs the Adventurer's Guild in Dalhurst and offers the full guild questline (quests 01-13)

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: Adventurer's Guild, Dalhurst chapter. Contracts come in, and I decide who I can send out without hearing about it afterwards. You looking for work?

choices.text: I want to join the guild.
The Beast of Millbrook is dead.
Willow Dale's deep section is cleared.
The ogre won't trouble the roads anymore.
I dealt with the Iron Blades.
The toll under the bridge is settled.
Do you have any contracts available?

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: I don't put the Guild's name on a stranger. There's a wolf pack denned on the Thornfield road that's killed two merchants this month, and nobody local will go near it. Clear it, come back and tell me, and we'll talk.

choices.text: Tell me more about this wolf problem.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: East of Dalhurst, off the Thornfield road. Two merchants dead this month, and my local hands have all suddenly found other work. Kill the pack and bring me something to show for it.

choices.text: I'm in. I'll clear them out.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: A hundred, a guild token, and your name on our books. After that you get first sight of the contracts instead of hearing about them in a tavern a week late.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: East of here, off the Thornfield road. Come back and tell me it's done. And don't die out there - dead men don't pay dues.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: You cleared the wolf pack? All eight of them? Let me see... Yes, this is the proof I needed. Well done. You've earned your place. Here's your payment - 100 gold and your guild token. Welcome to the Adventurer's Guild.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: Grain factor named Corrin Dale is losing a sack a night, and his own ratcatchers won't go past the loading doors anymore. He paid without arguing. Go and see what's in there.

choices.text: Rats? I expected something more challenging.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: Some of them are the size of dogs, and Corrin's men won't set foot inside. Small job, granted. It's still a man's living going out through a hole in his floor.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: The warehouse is down in the dock district. Watch for the nest - the big ones sit on it. Seventy-five when it's done.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: The warehouse is clear? The merchants are already singing your praises. Good work, Initiate. Here's your 75 gold. You're building a solid reputation. Ready for something more substantial?

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: Halvard has one wagon of dye going to Thornfield with this season's whole margin on it, bought on credit. Bandits have hit three caravans on that road. He paid our price without haggling, so I'm sending him someone who'll stay awake.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: Three caravans this month. Expect four or five of them, somewhere past the crossroads, and expect them interested - he's carrying dye, not turnips. Keep him breathing and the wagon loaded.

choices.text: I can handle bandits. I'll take the contract.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: He's at the east gate with the cart. They favour the crossroads for it. Bring him back in one piece and you're a Member.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: Halvard sent word ahead - he's singing your praises. Four bandits dead and not a scratch on his goods. Excellent work. Here's your 125 gold and more importantly - your badge as a full Guild Member. You've earned it.

choices.text: What contracts are available for Members?

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: The merchants have paid to end the raids out of the eastern outpost. The contract says eliminate. That's the word they asked for, and I'm the one who files it afterwards.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: Former soldier, and he's trained them like one. You can go at it in daylight, or you can go at it some other way. Either way the raids stop, and I'd rather not be told more than that.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: East of here. Do what the contract says, or near enough that I can sign it. Come and tell me yourself - don't send word.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: The eastern outpost. Tell me how it went, and tell me straight - I have to write it on a contract that says eliminate, and I would rather know what I am writing.

choices.text: I took the outpost apart. The captain is dead, as written.
I brought the captain back alive. He is the magistrate's problem now.
I took the captain alone and quietly. The rest scattered by morning.
They had already moved on when I got there.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: Three of mine went into Willow Dale two days ago and haven't come out. Find them. If you can't find them, bring me their tokens - the families get those.

choices.text: What were they hunting in Willow Dale?

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: Spider work. Routine, for them, and that's the part I keep turning over. Find out what went wrong, bring the tokens back, and if you get the chance, settle it.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: Willow Dale, northeast. They'd have gone for the nested sections. Three tokens is what the families need. The rest is up to you.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: You found them? And the tokens? Thank you. This... means a lot. To me, to their families. The spiders that did this - did you...?

choices.text: I killed every spider I found.
I recovered the tokens. That's what mattered.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: Good. Those bastards deserved it. Here's your 175 gold, and... thank you. The Guild remembers who takes care of our fallen. You're ready for Veteran work - something that'll test your real mettle.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: You're right. Bringing them home was what mattered. Here's your 175 gold. The Guild is in your debt. When you're ready for Veteran contracts, come see me.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: Millbrook has lost half its flocks since planting. A shepherd there, Ansel Crake, lost his last sheep two nights ago and won't take his cart out after dark. Three hunting parties out of that village have already missed it.

choices.text: What kind of creature is it?

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: Nobody's had a clear look at it. Talk to the elder - she's seen the tracks and she's seen what's left of the sheep. Whatever it is, it's been avoiding hunters, and that worries me more than the size of it.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: Millbrook is northwest. Elder first, tracks after. Bring me the pelt.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: A dire wolf alpha? By the gods, that explains the carnage. You tracked it to its lair and killed it? The Millbrook folk will sleep soundly tonight. Here's your 250 gold, the dire wolf cloak as a trophy, and your Veteran badge. You've earned every bit of it.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: A cave-in opened a stretch of Willow Dale nobody's mapped. I've heard - never mind where - that the Thieves Guild already put someone in there. Get in first. Whatever you carry out is yours.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: The upper levels were spiders and bandits. Below that, nobody knows. Assume undead, assume the builders left something behind a door, and assume yours isn't the only lamp down there.

choices.text: Undead and traps. I can handle it.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: The new entrance is on the eastern side. Map it, clear it. If you see anyone else's torchlight, I want to hear it from you before I hear it from them.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: You cleared the deep section? And found artifacts? Let me see... An ancient amulet. The mages would pay handsomely for this, but it's yours by contract. Here's your 300 gold and these enchanted explorer boots - they'll help you spot traps.

choices.text: I'll put these boots to good use.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: There's an ogre sitting on the Crossroads road taking coin off anyone who wants past. The merchants want it gone. Gone is the whole of what I was asked for.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: It's been charging rather than eating people, which means it can count and it can be talked to. Men have talked their way past worse. I'm not paying extra for a corpse.

choices.text: Let me think about the approach.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: Crossroads, on the main road. I don't care how the road comes clear. Come back and tell me which way you did it - straight.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: The ogre. How did it end?

choices.text: I talked to it. It is moving off the road.
I paid it. It is somebody else's ogre now.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: The Iron Blades have set up in Thornfield and they're taking work out from under us at half our rate. Go and settle it. I'd rather it were settled with words, and I'm not going to be particular.

choices.text: I'll deal with the Iron Blades.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: Their leader will fight you if you ask, and might listen if you don't. You could split the territory. You could run them out. You could bring them in with us, which I've never seen done and would like to.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: Thornfield. Find their leader. Anything that leaves the Guild standing is a result - but come back and tell me which one it was.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: You've resolved the Iron Blades situation? Tell me how.

choices.text: I defeated their leader in a duel.
I drove them out by force.
I paid them to take their contracts elsewhere.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: An alliance? That's... beyond what I hoped for. Two guilds working together. You've accomplished something remarkable. Here's your 400 gold and your Elite badge. The Guild will remember this.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: Negotiated boundaries? Pragmatic. Both guilds survive, territory is clear. Here's your 400 gold and your Elite badge. Well done.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: You defeated their leader in single combat? The traditional way. Respectful. Here's your 400 gold and your Elite badge.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: Drove them out by force? Effective, if brutal. The threat is eliminated. Here's your 400 gold and your Elite badge. The Guild appreciates results.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: Three separate reports this week put something winged over the Kazer-Dun quarry camp, and the stonecutters have stopped working the north face. If it's a dragon I pull that camp today. Go and look at it before I decide.

choices.text: Dragons are above my pay grade.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: A wyvern is dangerous. A dragon is a different conversation entirely, and I'd be evacuating rather than hiring. Get close enough to be certain and no closer - I want the answer, not another name for the board.

choices.text: I'll find out what's up there.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: Kazer-Dun. Track it to the nest and be sure of it. If it's a wyvern, bring me five scales. If it isn't, come back alive and say so.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: Wyvern scales? You found it and killed it? A wyvern, not a dragon - thank the gods. That's still an incredible feat. Here's your 500 gold and this dragonscale shield - crafted from the beast you slew. You've proven yourself beyond doubt.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: Sit down, and keep this between us. Contracts are being skimmed, bribes taken, and members have gone missing in ways I can't account for. Whoever it is has the run of my records, and you're the only one here who owes nobody.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: I have suspicions. I don't have anything I could say out loud without splitting this hall in half. Read the ledgers, talk to people quietly, find out who's been meeting whom - and be careful, they have friends.

choices.text: I need to think about this.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: Ledgers first. Then the members, carefully. When you're certain, confront them - and be ready for it to go badly.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: You found the traitor? Who was it, and what did you do?

choices.text: I exposed them. They're in custody now.
They offered me gold to stay quiet...
They resisted. I had no choice.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: Justice served properly. The Guild's reputation is restored, and members can trust us again. Here's your 450 gold, and more importantly - you've earned the rank of Guild Officer. Your name will be remembered.

choices.text: What's left for an officer to accomplish?

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: ...I see. I'm disappointed, but I understand the temptation. The corruption remains hidden for now. Here's your official payment. We'll speak no more of this.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: Dead traitors tell no tales, but they also can't name their contacts. Still, the threat is eliminated. Here's your 450 gold. The Guild is grateful.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: There's a contract on that board older than my time here, and everyone who's tried it is dead. I'm calling it in now because the Iron Blades bought a key-fragment map off a fence in Thornfield. Whoever opens that door first keeps every client who'd pay for work like it.

choices.text: If everyone fails, why should I try?

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: Three key fragments, scattered through Willow Dale. Behind the door is a guardian the builders were frightened enough of to seal in. And behind that, the Blade of Legends.

choices.text: The Blade of Legends? I'm in.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: Because you're not everyone else who tried. You've put down a wyvern and a dire wolf and walked out of that place twice already. I'm not going to make you go.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: The fragments are in the upper levels. Unseal the door, kill what's behind it, take the blade. Come back and we'll talk about the last thing.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: By the gods... You did it. The Blade of Legends. The Ancient Guardian defeated. You've accomplished what no one else could. Here's your 750 gold and this Legendary Adventurer's Cloak. But there's one more thing.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: There's one thing left, and it's me. Nobody below me would fight you honestly, and there's nobody above me. Beat me in the ring and the title is yours, along with first pick of everything that comes through that door.

choices.text: I need more time to prepare.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: I haven't fought a real bout in six years and I don't much want to start now. But I'm not handing the Champion's title to a man I haven't tested, and I'm not asking anyone else to lose to you politely.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: The arena, then. Come and find me when you're ready - and don't be gentle about it. I'd know, and it would go worse for you.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: You put me on the floor of my own hall. Six years I've been telling people I could still do this. Here's a thousand, the Champion's Circlet, and my axe - it goes with the title, and I'd rather hand it over than have it taken.

choices.text: What are my duties as Champion?

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: As Champion, you represent the Guild's martial excellence. You'll handle disputes of honor, train promising recruits, and take first pick of elite contracts. The bounty board is always available for you. The Guild salutes you, Champion.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: The honor is mine, Champion. The Guild is stronger with you leading its warriors. Return whenever you want elite contracts or bounty work.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: Board's on the wall. It changes daily and I don't hold jobs for anyone.

choices.text: Do you have any personal recommendations?

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: Let me see what contracts match your current standing...

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: As Champion, you have access to unlimited bounty contracts. Check the board anytime for monster hunts, bandit clearing, and escort missions. The work never stops for someone of your caliber.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: We put fighters in front of other people's problems for a fee. Merchants, towns, the occasional noble who wants a thing handled without his name on it. The Guild's name is the only thing I actually sell, so I am careful who wears it.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: This is adventuring work, not temple charity. Violence comes with the territory. Complete your current contracts and more options will open up.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: Then the guild isn't for you. Come back if you change your mind.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: Welcome aboard, Initiate. Return when you're ready for work.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: Congratulations on Member rank. Contracts await when you're ready.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: Well earned, Veteran. The dangerous work awaits.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: Good hunting. And remember - the guild always gets its cut.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: As written. Good. That is the version the merchants paid for and the version I can put my name under without thinking about it afterwards. Two hundred, and you are somebody I can hand the awkward ones to now.

choices.text: I will take a break first.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: Alive. ... The merchants are going to hang him in the square and charge for a view of it, and every one of them will feel better about themselves for having had a trial first. It is not what the contract said. It is what the contract meant. Two hundred, and I will be the one explaining the difference.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: One throat and a camp that woke up leaderless. The raids stop, nobody the Guild has to feed, nobody's widow at my door in a month. Between us, Member - that is the best possible answer and I could never have asked for it out loud. Two hundred.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: Moved on. ... I have been doing this a long time, and 'they had already gone' is what a man says when he wants the money and does not want the conversation. Take your two hundred. I am writing 'dispersed' on the contract, and I am writing your name beside it, and if those raids start again on that road I will remember both.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: Killed. Clean and final and the caravans are already rolling. Here is your three hundred and fifty. Now - I have a delicate matter that needs a veteran's touch. Guild politics.

choices.text: I will hear about it later.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: You talked to it. People will not believe that and I am not going to correct them, because a Guild that can end a thing without killing it is worth more per contract than one that cannot. Three hundred and fifty. There is a delicate matter next - guild politics.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: Paid it. So there is now an ogre on somebody else's road with a taste for being paid, and in six months a guild in another town takes a contract about it. That is how this works and I am not going to pretend otherwise. Three hundred and fifty. Next matter is guild politics.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: You bought them off. With your own coin, I notice, since none of mine is missing. The Iron Blades are gone, and they are gone owing you a favour, which is a strange thing for a rival guild to be. Four hundred and your Elite badge. I am not certain whether I have promoted a diplomat or a man with a rival guild in his pocket.

choices.text: What is next for an Elite?

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: The bridge toll. How did you settle it?

choices.text: Killed it. The bridge is clear.
Intimidated it. It won't be back.
Paid it off. It's somebody else's toll now.
Negotiated a fair toll. It collects, we watch.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: Dead troll, clear bridge. That's the straightforward answer, and most of these contracts end there. Three hundred gold. The merchants will be loud about it so I don't have to be.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: Talked it down without spending a coin. Not bad. Trolls remember fear longer than they remember gold, so it might even stay gone. Three hundred, and a bit more besides - the Guild likes a contract that costs nothing but nerve.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: Paid it. So there's a troll loose on somebody's road with a taste for coin now, same as that ogre. The merchants will hear you solved it with their money and they won't love that part. Three hundred, and don't expect me to call it clever twice.

nodes.speaker: Guildmaster Vorn
nodes.text: A toll it collects and we watch. That's the answer I'd have wanted and wouldn't have dared write into the contract. The merchants get a bridge they can cross for a fair price, and the troll gets to keep being a troll. Three hundred, and this is the one I'll tell people about.
